key_insight: Human and LLM-designed synthesis recipes can achieve comparable lab success, and their closed-loop collaboration led to discovery of a new material prototype.
engineering_relevance: This workflow shows how AI can accelerate materials synthesis planning for hard-to-predict compounds, especially when paired with experimental feedback.
method: Generated synthesis recipes with humans and LLMs for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials.
Tested each recipe in the lab and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration.
Compared round-one and round-two success rates to assess learning and iteration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports similar experimental success rates for humans and LLMs across known and unknown targets in two rounds, with a newly discovered material, Ba3PtO5, emerging from the process.
watch_item: Success drops sharply for unknown materials, so generalization beyond the studied phase space may still be limited and needs careful validation.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
